You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS • There are forty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. • For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Write in soft pencil. • Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. • Do not use correction fluid. • Do not write on any bar codes. • You may use a calculator. INFORMATION • The total mark for this paper is 40. • Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. • Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

The diagram shows a protein molecule. globular head key long polypeptide short polypeptide Two long polypeptides each form α-helices for much of their length and these twist together into a fibre. At one end, each of these polypeptides coils into a globular head. Two short polypeptides bind to each globular head. What describes the protein structure of this molecule?

options.A: quaternary structure because each molecule consists of six polypeptides
options.B: secondary structure because the long polypeptides form α-helices
options.C: tertiary structure because the α-helices form a fibre
options.D: tertiary structure because the heads form globular proteins

questions.questionText: Which types of bond will keep a folded protein in its precise shape for the longest time as the temperature rises?

options.A: disulfide

questions.questionText: An enzyme is modified for industrial use. It has a lower Michaelis-Menten constant (K ) than the m unmodified enzyme. What is true of the modified enzyme?

options.A: It is more specific.
options.B: It has a higher affinity for its substrate.
options.C: It has a lower maximum rate of reaction (V ). max
options.D: It needs more substrate to become saturated.

options.C: • proportion of phospholipids with saturated fatty acid chains • proportion of long fatty acid chains
options.D: • proportion of phospholipids with unsaturated fatty acid chains • temperature

options.A: They are undifferentiated cells that are present at birth.
options.B: They differentiate to form skin cells.
options.C: They divide by mitosis to supply some cells that can differentiate.
options.D: They have the full number of chromosomes.

questions.questionText: Scientists grew bacteria in a medium containing heavy nitrogen, 15N, as the only source of nitrogen. After many generations, all of the bacterial DNA contained heavy nitrogen. These bacteria were then moved from the heavy nitrogen medium into a medium with only light nitrogen, 14N. Some bacteria were collected from each of the next three generations and their DNA was analysed. Hybrid DNA contains both heavy and light nitrogen. Which row shows the correct DNA of the first and third generations? DNA of first generation DNA of third generation

options.A: all hybrid half hybrid, half light
options.B: all hybrid one quarter hybrid, three quarters light
options.C: half hybrid, half heavy half hybrid, one quarter heavy, one quarter light
options.D: half hybrid, half light one quarter hybrid, three quarters light

However, some bacteria in the population have an allele coding for an enzyme that breaks down penicillin. These bacteria are able to survive. Which could explain how these bacterial cells acquired this allele?

questions.questionText: A number of processes contribute to maintaining a water potential gradient in plants allowing water to reach the highest parts of a plant. Which processes are responsible for maintaining this water potential gradient?
What is a correct statement about the movement of substances absorbed by roots?

options.A: Ions have to pass through cell walls to cross the endodermis.
options.B: Ions move through the symplastic pathway only until they reach the Casparian strip.
options.C: Soil water has a more negative water potential than the xylem sap.
options.D: Water passes through the symplastic pathway along a water potential gradient.

questions.questionText: Which statement about sucrose loading into companion cells and then into the phloem sieve tube element is not correct?

options.A: Hydrogen ions and sucrose molecules move into the companion cells using a carrier protein.
options.B: Hydrogen ions are pumped out of the companion cells by active transport.
options.C: Sucrose molecules are carried into the companion cells down the concentration gradient for sucrose.
options.D: Sucrose molecules move from a companion cell into the sieve tubes of the phloem through plasmodesmata.

questions.questionText: What explains why the left and right sides of the heart contract simultaneously?

options.A: Both atria have a sinoatrial node.
options.B: Both sides of the heart are supplied by the same coronary artery.
options.C: Purkyne tissue links the two sides of the heart.
options.D: There is no barrier to electrical excitation between two sides of the heart.
